ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r9.claim: Nuṭfa is a small quantity of water; semen is called this because it drips one drop after another.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p172/r9.anchor: النطفة القليل من الماء، يقال ما في القربة من الماء نطفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177#2/r1.claim: The reminder that God made him a man may mean He gave him a balanced, sound body and completed his growth; it may also mean He made him male rather than female.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177#2/r1.anchor: وقيل: ذكره بنعمة الله عليه في كونه رجلا ولم يخلقه أنثى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177#2/r2.claim: The successive stages of creation demonstrate God's complete power and that nothing is beyond Him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177#2/r2.anchor: نبهه بهذه التنقلات على كمال قدرته وأنه لا يعجزه شيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177#2/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177#2/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī glosses sawāka rajulan as making him well-proportioned, complete, male, and mature.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177#2/r3.anchor: سواك عدلك وكملك إنسانا ذكرا بالغا مبلغ الرجال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177#2/r4.claim: Rajulan is a circumstantial accusative; al-Ḥawfī instead treats it as a second object of sawwā.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177#2/r4.anchor: وانتصب رجلا على الحال. وقال الحوفي رجلا نصب بسوى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177#2/r5.claim: The question is not a request for information but a rebuke that effectively affirms the man's disbelief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177#2/r5.anchor: ولما لم يكن الاستفهام استفهام استعلام وإنما هو استفهام إنكار وتوبيخ

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p172/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p172/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p172/r1.claim: The believer reminds his companion that his origin was earth and a drop, after which God fashioned him as a sound, upright man.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r1.claim: The companion’s speech is introduced with قال without a conjunction because it functions as the question-and-answer turn in the dialogue.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r1.anchor: حكي كلام صاحبه بفعل القول بدون عطف للدلالة على أنه واقع موقع المحاورة والمجاوبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r2.claim: The question about disbelief expresses astonishment and censure, not a genuine inquiry, since the companion knew the other was a polytheist.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r2.anchor: والاستفهام في قوله : { أكفرت بالذي خلقك } مستعمل في التعجب والإنكار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r3.claim: Here kufr means associating partners with God, including denial of resurrection; the relative clause invokes God’s creation to expose the addressee’s ignorance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r3.anchor: فالمراد بالكفر هنا الإشراك الذي من جملة معتقداته إنكار البعث ، ولذلك عرف بطريق الموصولية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r4.claim: The clause argues that people acknowledge God created them, so no other being deserves worship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r4.anchor: فإنهم يعترفون بأن الله هو الذي خلق الناس فما كان غير الله مستحقا للعبادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r5.claim: Knowledge of the first creation should prevent denial of the second, as cited in 50:15 and 30:27; the wording therefore insinuates the addressee’s ignorance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r5.anchor: ثم إن العلم بالخلق الأول من شأنه أن يصرف الإنسان عن إنكار الخلق الثاني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r6.claim: From dust points to the food components extracted from earth that make up the drop of semen, with 36:36 cited in support.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r6.anchor: من تراب } إشارة إلى الأجزاء التي تتكون منها النطفة وهي أجزاء الأغذية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r7.claim: Nutfah means a man’s fluid and derives from a root meaning to flow.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r7.anchor: والنطفة : ماء الرجل ، مشتقة من النطف وهو السيلان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r8.claim: Sawwāka means he fashioned you proportionately in form and function.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r8.anchor: و سواك } عدل خلقك ، أي جعله متناسبا في الشكل والعمل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r9.claim: The preposition min in from dust and then from a drop marks origin.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p321#3/r9.anchor: و ( من ) في قوله : { من تراب ثم من نطفة } ابتدائية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516#3/r7.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516#3/r7.claim: Ubayy b. Kaʿb reads the companion as disputing with the unbeliever.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516#3/r8.speaker: ثابت البناني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516#3/r8.claim: Thabit al-Bunani reads an added rebuke: Woe to you, have you disbelieved?

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516#3/r9.claim: From dust points to Adam; making him a man may simply mean a person or living being, or may highlight the blessing of being male, as al-Tabari also suggests.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p516#3/r9.anchor: وقوله من تراب إشارة إلى آدم عليه السلام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p158/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p158/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p158/r1.claim: The believer's question rebukes the garden owner for denying the God who created him from dust through Adam and then from a drop of humble fluid; the statement affirms God's sole lordship and worship.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p158/r1.anchor: وهذا إنكار وتعظيم لما وقع فيه من جحود ربه، الذي خلقه وابتدأ خلق الإنسان من طين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p158/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p158/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p158/r2.claim: As 2:280 asks how people can disbelieve after being lifeless and brought to life, everyone knows they once did not exist and could not create themselves or derive existence from another created thing; this plainly points to God as Creator.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p158/r2.anchor: فإنه ما من أحد من المخلوقات إلا ويعلم أنه كان معدوما ثم وجد، وليس وجوده من نفسه

JISHUMI:v6p4413/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4413/r5.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v6p4413/r5.claim: Knowledge of God is not necessary or self-evident; the brother's argument shows religious reasoning is valid.
JISHUMI:v6p4413/r5.anchor: أن المعارف ليست ضرورة، عن أبي علي ويستدل على أن أخاه حاجه لذلك

JISHUMI:v6p4413/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4413/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4413/r6.claim: The brother's address as one who debates him supports the validity of argument in religion.
JISHUMI:v6p4413/r6.anchor: قال: يحاوره فتدل على صحة الحجاج في الدين

JISHUMI:v6p4415/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4415/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4415/r11.claim: The believer argues that God created the man's ancestor Adam from soil, then his offspring from a sperm drop and fashioned him into a sound man; these changes prove a wise, pre-eternal Creator.
JISHUMI:v6p4415/r11.anchor: خلق ولده من نطفة ثم سواك رجلا أي: عدلك

TABATABAI:18:36-39/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:36-39/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:36-39/r4.claim: The believer answers two boasts: the man’s assumed independence over God and his scorn for his companion’s lesser wealth and followers; the reply addresses the first through 18:38 and the second through the later garden comparison.
TABATABAI:18:36-39/r4.anchor: وقد حلل الكلام من حيث غرض المتكلم إلى جهتين إحداهما استعلاؤه على الله

TABATABAI:18:36-39/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:36-39/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:36-39/r5.claim: Repeating that the companion was conversing with him shows his faith and composure remained steady; he speaks gently and avoids insulting the man’s children, only hinting that the garden could fail.
TABATABAI:18:36-39/r5.anchor: إشارة إلى أنه لم ينقلب عما كان عليه من سكينة الإيمان ووقاره

TABATABAI:18:36-39/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:36-39/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:36-39/r6.claim: “Have you disbelieved in the Creator?” condemns the man’s shirk: claiming independence for oneself and worldly causes; that same stance feeds his doubt about resurrection.
TABATABAI:18:36-39/r6.anchor: ينكر عليه ما اشتمل عليه كلامه من الشرك بالله سبحانه بدعوى الاستقلال لنفسه

TABATABAI:18:36-39/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:36-39/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:36-39/r7.claim: Against al-Zamakhsharī, the author says the man is not an idol-worshipping polytheist who outright denied resurrection: he calls God “my Lord” and only doubts or deems resurrection unlikely.
TABATABAI:18:36-39/r7.anchor: ولو كان كما قال لذكر فيه الإيمان بالمعاد

TABRISI:18:37-44/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:37-44/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:37-44/r1.claim: Readers differ over لكنّا: Ibn ʿĀmir, Ibn Fulayḥ, al-Barjamī, Yaʿqūb, and Warsh in one form retain the alif in connection and pause; most drop it in connection, and the pause form keeps it save for Qutaybah.
TABRISI:18:37-44/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وابن فليح والبرجمي ويعقوب لكنا بإثبات الألف

TABRISI:18:37-44/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:37-44/r2.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:18:37-44/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives لكن from لكن أنا by deleting the hamza and assimilating two nūns; the alif of أنا normally disappears in connection, though some dialects retain it.
TABRISI:18:37-44/r2.anchor: من قرأ لكن بتشديد النون فهو لكن أنا في الأصل

TABRISI:18:37-44/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:37-44/r3.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:18:37-44/r3.claim: Abu Ali disputes that the retained alif is a desirable substitute for the lost hamza: it behaves like a pausal letter and should not be pronounced in connected recitation.
TABRISI:18:37-44/r3.anchor: لا أرى قوله أن إثبات الألف هو الجيد لأنه صار عوضا من الهمزة

TABRISI:18:37-44/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:37-44/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:37-44/r4.claim: The anomalous readings لكن أنا and لكن هو الله ربي parse respectively with أنا as the subject of a sentence and هو as a pronoun of the matter or story, as in the quoted verses.
TABRISI:18:37-44/r4.anchor: وقراءة عيسى الثقفي لكن هو الله ربي

TABRISI:18:37-44#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:37-44#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:37-44#2/r1.claim: For retained-alif لكنّا, one grammatical account assimilates the nūn of لكن to the attached pronoun, which then takes a fixed alif; another treats the alif like a pausal extension analogous to a pausal hāʾ.
TABRISI:18:37-44#2/r1.anchor: ومن قرأ لكنا في الوصل فإنه يحتمل أمرين

TABRISI:18:37-44#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:37-44#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:37-44#2/r2.claim: The reading with هو uses the pronoun of the matter, so the sentence means ‘the matter is: God is my Lord’; the returned pronoun appears in ربي.
TABRISI:18:37-44#2/r2.anchor: والوجه الآخر أن سيبويه حكى أنه سمع من يقول أعطني أبيضه

THALABI:v6p170#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p170#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p170#2/r4.claim: The companion's question about creation recalls that God created the man's father and origin from dust, then the man from a drop and fashioned him upright as a male human.
THALABI:v6p170#2/r4.anchor: خلق أباك وأصلك من تراب ثم خلقك من نطفة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:37-41/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:37-41/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:37-41/r1.claim: The interlocutor reminds his companion that God created him from dust, then a sperm drop in his mother's womb, and made him an upright man.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:37-41/r1.anchor: في رحم أمك { ثم سواك رجلا }

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p186/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p186/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p186/r2.claim: The believing companion challenges the owner for disbelieving in the Creator, who first made humankind from dust (Adam), then a drop, and fashioned him as a man.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p186/r2.anchor: } وهو يحاوره أكفرت بالذي خلقك من تراب { [الكهف: 37] يعني أول خلق الإنسان، يعني آدم.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The parable mirrors Quraysh’s outward and inward arrogance and the conflict between truth and falsehood; the poor companion has faith and joy in knowing God despite lacking orchards.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The arrogant among the Quraysh are narrated a parable here which mirrors their inner and outer selves and also makes them see the fate of the conflict between truth and falsehood

BURSEVI:v5p190#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p190#2/r5.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v5p190#2/r5.claim: The circumstantial phrase about their dialogue alerts the listener that the ensuing speech is important to the exchange.
BURSEVI:v5p190#2/r5.anchor: وفائدة هذه الجملة الحالية التنبيه من الأمر الأول على أن ما يتلوه كلام معتنى بشأنه

BURSEVI:v5p190#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p190#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p190#2/r6.claim: The believer's question treats denial of resurrection as doubt in God's attributes and power; the man derives through Adam from dust, then from his mother's sperm, and is shaped upright as an adult male.
BURSEVI:v5p190#2/r6.anchor: أي : من مني في رحم أمك ثانيا وهي مادتك القريبة

BURSEVI:v5p191/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p191/r1.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v5p191/r1.claim: The lexicon says rajul is the familiar word for a man, or specifically a male who has reached puberty and grown up.
BURSEVI:v5p191/r1.anchor: قال في "القاموس" الرجل بضم الجيم وسكونها معروف

ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r1.claim: The dialogue framing is an independent circumstantial clause that signals the ensuing exchange is carefully presented as conversation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r1.anchor: جملة حالية كالسابقة وفائدتها التنبيه من أول الأمر على أن ما يتلوها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r2.speaker: أبي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r2.claim: Ubayy’s explanatory reading replaces yuḥāwiruhu with yukhāṣimuhu, he was disputing with him.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبي وحمل ذلك على التفسير ( وهو يخاصمه )

ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r3.claim: The unbeliever was created from soil through Adam, whose constitution contained humankind’s pattern, so the attribution is real through his origin.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r3.anchor: أي في ضمن خلق أصلك منه وهو آدم عليه السلام لما أن خلق كل فرد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r4.claim: Another explanation traces his material to soil because male fluid develops from food whose sources return to soil, a figurative attribution from cause to effect.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r4.anchor: وقيل خلقك منه لأنه أصل مادتك إذ ماء الرجل يتولد من أغذية راجعة إلى التراب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r5.claim: A report says an angel puts soil into each sperm destined to become human; al-Ālūsī recalls possible authentication but notes problems applying it here.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r5.anchor: ونقل أنه ما من نطفة قدر الله تعالى أن يخلق منها بشرا إلا وملك موكل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r6.claim: The sperm is the nearer material origin; one person is made from successive origins. Taswiya means proportioning and perfecting in a balanced form.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r6.anchor: هي مادتك القريبة فالمخلوق واحد والمبدأ متعدد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r7.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān parses rajulan as a circumstantial accusative; al-Ḥawfī instead takes it as a second object and stresses God made him male.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r7.anchor: على ما قال أبو حيان على الحال وهو محوج إلى التأويل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r8.speaker: الحوفي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r8.claim: Al-Ḥawfī parses rajulan as the second object of sawwā, emphasizing that God made him a man.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r8.anchor: وقال الحوفي : نصب على أنه مفعول ثان لسوى

ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r9.claim: The charge of disbelief answers doubt about resurrection, entailing doubt about God’s power, truthfulness, and wisdom; linked to 23:115.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r9.anchor: ألا ترى إلى قوله عز وجل ( أفحسبتم أنما خلقناكم عبثا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r10.claim: Other commentators take him to have been an idolater; akafarta then means did you associate partners, since acknowledging a Lord does not exclude idolatry.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p276#2/r10.anchor: وقال بعضهم : الظاهر إنه كان مشركا كما يدل عليه قول صاحبه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p277/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p277/r1.speaker: ثابت البناني
ALUSI-FULL:v15p277/r1.claim: Thābit al-Bunānī reads waylaka akafarta, adding woe to you as an explanatory reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p277/r1.anchor: وقرأ ثابت البناني وحمل ذلك على التفسير

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:37/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:37/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:37/r1.claim: Dust is the source material of the man himself or his first ancestor; sperm is his immediate material, and God then completed him as an adult male.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:37/r1.anchor: ثم عدلك وكملك إنسانا ذكرا بالغا مبلغ الرجال

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:37/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:37/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:37/r2.claim: Denying resurrection amounts to disbelief in God because it doubts His power; creating man from dust establishes His ability to recreate him from it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:37/r2.anchor: جعل كفره بالبعث كفرا بالله تعالى لأن منشأه الشك في كمال قدرة الله تعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v4p444/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p444/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p444/r3.claim: The two-garden story concerns two Israelites: one is deceived by wealth and assumes permanence, while his believing companion relies on God; the garden disappears and regret remains.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p444/r3.anchor: وقد أفصحت هذه الآي منها باغترار أحدهما بما لديه وركونه إلى توهم البقاء

BIQAI-FULL:v4p444/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p444/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p444/r4.claim: The ruined garden illustrates that whoever relies on anything besides God loses it, since everything perishes except Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p444/r4.anchor: وهذه حال من ركن إلى ما سوى المالك , ومن كل شيء إلا وجهه سبحانه وتعالى فان وهالك

BIQAI-FULL:v4p467/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p467/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p467/r11.claim: The companion rebukes him for denying resurrection, citing creation from soil, then sperm, then a fully formed man as proof God can recreate him.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p467/r11.anchor: { أكفرت } . ولما كان كفره بإنكار البعث , دل عليه بقوله تعالى : { بالذي خلقك من تراب }

BIQAI-FULL:v4p467/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p467/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p467/r12.claim: The man accepts resurrection only as a doubtful hypothetical despite its decisive basis; making death life's endpoint would deprive obedient and sinful people of recompense.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p467/r12.anchor: ولم تثبت لها في الإعادة ما ثبت لها بعلمك في الابتداء , ثم لم تجوزها بعد القطع بالنفي إلا على سبيل الفرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r4.claim: The narrative is more likely historical: its unprefixed dialogue and the later report of the man's defeat resemble remembered events and make the warning more forceful.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p316/r4.anchor: والأظهر من سياق الكلام وصنع التراكيب مثل قوله : قال له صاحبه وهو يحاوره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p319/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p319/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p319/r1.claim: The dialogue shows the poorer man had admonished his companion about faith and righteous conduct; the rich man answered with arrogance rather than fair argument.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p319/r1.anchor: ودل فعل المحاورة على أن صاحبه قد وعظه في الإيمان والعمل الصالح ، فراجعه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p143/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p143/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p143/r1.claim: The companion is the believer, who asks whether the other has disbelieved in the Creator: Adam was made from dust, then the man from a sperm drop; doubting resurrection makes him an unbeliever.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p143/r1.anchor: يعني المؤمن وهو يحاوره أكفرت بالذي خلقك من تراب يعني خلق أباك آدم ثم من نطفة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675/r1.claim: Creating the addressee from dust means creating his origin, since creating the origin causes his own creation and is therefore attributed to him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675/r1.anchor: أي خلق أصلك ، لأن خلق أصله سبب في خلقه ، فكان خلقه خلقا له

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675/r2.claim: Sawwāka means proportioned and completed him as a male human who reached adulthood.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675/r2.anchor: عدلك وكملك إنسانا ذكرا بالغا مبلغ الرجال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675/r3.claim: His doubt about resurrection makes him an unbeliever in God and a denier of His blessings, just as denying a Messenger makes one an unbeliever.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p675/r3.anchor: جعله كافرا بالله جاحدا لأنعمه لشكه في البعث ، كما يكون المكذب بالرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم كافرا

MUQATIL:18:34-37/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:34-37/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:34-37/r10.claim: The believer rebukes his companion for disbelief in the Creator who made him from earth, meaning Adam, then from a drop and fashioned him as a man.
MUQATIL:18:34-37/r10.anchor: يعني آدم، عليه السلام؛ لأن أول خلقه التراب، ثم قال

NASAFI-FULL:v3p14#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p14#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p14#3/r1.claim: ‘Created from dust’ refers to his ancestor, whose creation caused his own; he was then created from a drop and formed into a complete, adult male human.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p14#3/r1.anchor: وكان خلقه خلقاله ﴿ ثم من نطفة ﴾ أي خلقك من نطفة ﴿ ثم سواك رجلا ﴾ عدلك وكملك انسانا ذكرا بالغا مبلغ الرجال

NASAFI-FULL:v3p14#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p14#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p14#3/r2.claim: The companion asks whether he has disbelieved in his Creator by doubting resurrection.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p14#3/r2.anchor: جعله كافرا بالله لشكه في البعث

QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r1.claim: The believing companion is named Judah or Tamlīkha, depending on the disagreement over identity.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r1.anchor: يهوذا أو تمليخا على الخلاف في اسمه.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r2.claim: The companion argues that creation from earth, then a drop, and finally a formed man is more extraordinary than resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r2.anchor: وعظه وبين له أن ما اعترف به من هذه الأشياء التي لا ينكرها أحد أبدع من الإعادة.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r3.claim: Making him a man means giving him upright stature and form, sound limbs, and male sex.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r3.anchor: و «سواك رجلا» أي جعلك معتدل القامة والخلق، صحيح الأعضاء ذكرا.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي وأبو العالية
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r4.claim: Al-Sulami and Abu al-Aliya read لكنا هو الله ربي with the long alif retained.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r4.anchor: { لكنا هو الله ربي } كذا قرأه أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي وأبو العالية.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r5.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r5.claim: Al-Kisai also transmits لكن هو الله, supplying an omitted noun: rather, the matter is that God is my Lord.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r5.anchor: وروي عن الكسائي { لكن هو الله } بمعنى لكن الأمر هو الله ربي،

QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r6.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r6.claim: Al-Kisai explains common لكنا by reordered لكن الله هو ربي أنا, with hamza and alif dropped and the two nuns assimilated.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r6.anchor: قال الكسائي: فيه تقديم وتأخير، تقديره: لكن الله هو ربي أنا،

QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r7.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r7.claim: Al-Nahhas records al-Kisai, al-Farra, and al-Mazini's analysis: لكن أنا contracts by moving the hamza vowel, deleting hamza, and assimilating nuns.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r7.anchor: وقال النحاس: مذهب الكسائي والفراء والمازني أن الأصل لكن أنا

QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r8.speaker: أبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r8.claim: Abu Ubayd derives the form from لكن أنا, with the dropped alif bringing two nuns together; al-Kisai cites poetry.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r8.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد: الأصل لكن أنا، فحذفت الألف فالتقت نونان فجاء بالتشديد لذلك،

QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r9.speaker: أبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r9.claim: Abu Hatim calls Asim's connected alif ungrammatical; al-Zajjaj says it compensates for أنا's deleted alif, and Ubay reads لكن أنا هو الله ربي.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r9.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم: ورووا عن عاصم «لكنا هو الله ربي» وزعم أن هذا لحن،

QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r10.speaker: ابن عامر والمسيلي عن نافع ورويس عن يعقوب
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r10.claim: These readers retain the alif both at pause and in connected recitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38/r10.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر والمسيلي عن نافع ورويس عن يعقوب «لكنا» في حال الوقف والوصل معا بإثبات الألف.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38#2/r1.claim: A poetic citation completes the evidence for retaining the alif; Qurtubi says there is no disagreement about it at pause.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38#2/r1.anchor: بعد المشيب كفى ذاك عارا ولا خلاف في إثباتها في الوقف.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38#2/r2.claim: هو is a pronoun of story or affair, as in 21:79 and the opening of al-Ikhlas.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38#2/r2.anchor: «هو» ضمير القصة والشأن والأمر كقوله فإذا هي شاخصة أبصار الذين كفروا

QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38#2/r3.claim: Refusing to associate anyone with God implies the other man was a polytheist; alternatively wealth and poverty come from God, or denial of resurrection makes Him seem powerless by likening Him to creation.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:37-38#2/r3.anchor: دل مفهومه على أن الأخ الآخر كان مشركا بالله تعالى يعبد غيره.

MAJAZ:v1p403/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p403/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p403/r1.claim: يحاوره means speaks with him, from محاورة (conversation).
MAJAZ:v1p403/r1.anchor: «وهو يحاوره» (37) أي يكلمه، ومعناه من المحاورة

RAZI-FULL:v21p107/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p107/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p107/r1.claim: The believer's question ‘Have you disbelieved?’ establishes that doubting resurrection is unbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v21p107/r1.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن الشاك في حصول البعث كافر

RAZI-FULL:v21p107/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p107/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p107/r2.claim: The first argument for resurrection is that the God who created a person initially can recreate him.
RAZI-FULL:v21p107/r2.anchor: لما قدر على الابتداء وجب أن يقدر على الإعادة

RAZI-FULL:v21p107/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p107/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p107/r3.claim: A second argument is that God made humans for worship rather than in vain, entailing reward and punishment; rational adulthood prepares one for obligation, so abandonment would be unreasonable.
RAZI-FULL:v21p107/r3.anchor: لما خلقك هكذا فلم يخلقك عبثا

STUDYQURAN:18:37/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:37/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:37/r1.claim: Human origination from dust and then a drop signals human lowliness before God; elsewhere these stages describe human development.
STUDYQURAN:18:37/r1.anchor: is understood as an indication of human beings’ lowliness, especially in relation to God

STUDYQURAN:18:37/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:37/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:37/r2.claim: Fashioning a person as a man means shaping him as a mature individual and endowing him with intelligence and religious responsibility (taklīf).
STUDYQURAN:18:37/r2.anchor: Fashioned you as a man refers to God’s having further shaped him as a mature individual

TABATABAI:18:37-38/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:37-38/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:37-38/r1.claim: All human capacities and effects, from dust and semen to mature personhood, are wholly God's gift; neither people nor natural causes own these independently, so the believer rebukes the man's denial of divine lordship.
TABATABAI:18:37-38/r1.anchor: فليس للإنسان أن يستقل عنه تعالى في شيء من نفسه وآثار نفسه ولا لشيء من الأسباب الكونية ذلك

TABATABAI:18:37-38/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:37-38/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:37-38/r2.claim: The companion's appeal to the man's origin in dust and semen shows that his mature humanity and powers were bestowed by God, leaving no basis for self-sufficiency.
TABATABAI:18:37-38/r2.anchor: يقول إنك ذاك التراب ثم المني الذي ما كان يملك من الإنسانية والرجولية وآثار ذلك شيئا

TABRISI:18:37-38/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:37-38/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:37-38/r5.claim: The believer rebukes disbelief in the Creator, who made the interlocutor's father Adam from dust.
TABRISI:18:37-38/r5.anchor: يعني أصل الخلقة أي خلق أباك من تراب وهو آدم

TABRISI:18:37-38/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:37-38/r6.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:18:37-38/r6.claim: Because food grows from soil and produces the fluid by which people are ordinarily created, creation from dust is apt language.
TABRISI:18:37-38/r6.anchor: لما كانت النطفة خلقها الله سبحانه بمجرى العادة

TABRISI:18:37-38/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:37-38/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:37-38/r7.claim: God moved him from state to state until making him a human being with balanced form and stature.
TABRISI:18:37-38/r7.anchor: نقلك من حال إلى حال حتى جعلك بشرا معتدل الخلقة والقامة

TABRISI:18:37-38/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:37-38/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:37-38/r8.claim: The garden owner's disbelief consisted in denying resurrection; the passage treats doubt about resurrection as unbelief.
TABRISI:18:37-38/r8.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على أن الشك في البعث والنشور كفر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p16/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p16/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p16/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Adam was created from dust; his descendant came from a drop, and because his father was from dust, the man too is from dust.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p16/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد أن آدم خلق من تراب)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p16/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p16/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p16/r2.claim: Nutfa literally means water; people call a small amount in a waterskin a nutfa, and Arabs use the term for either little or much water.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p16/r2.anchor: ومعنى النطفة في اللغة: الماء، يقال: في القربة نطفة من ماء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p16/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p16/r3.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p16/r3.claim: Al-Azhari says Arabs use nutfa for both a small and a large quantity of water.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p16/r3.anchor: قال الأزهري: (والعرب تقول للماء القليل والكثير: نطفة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p16/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p16/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p16/r4.claim: God calls semen a nutfa, as in the verse about a drop of semen being emitted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p16/r4.anchor: وسمى الله عز وجل المني نطفة قال: {ألم يك نطفة من مني

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p16/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p16/r5.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p16/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi explains 'then fashioned you a man' as making him proportionate, fully formed, and sound in limbs and senses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p16/r5.anchor: قال الكلبي: (جعلك معتد الخلق والقامة, صحيح اليدين، والرجلين، والعينين)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p16/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p16/r6.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p16/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj glosses it as completing the man; the author prefers this because Arabic says a youth has matured and become fully grown, as in the verse about Moses reaching maturity.

SAMIN-DURR:18:37/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:37/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:37/r1.claim: Nuṭfa originally means a drop of clear water, from naṭafa ‘to drip’; a hadith says ‘his head dripped,’ with a variant ‘it poured’ explaining it, and semen is called a drop by analogy.
SAMIN-DURR:18:37/r1.anchor: النطفة في الأصل: القطرة من الماء الصافي يقال: نطف ينطف، أي: قطر

SAMIN-DURR:18:37/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:37/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:37/r2.claim: Rajulan may be circumstantial despite being neither derived nor transient, since it follows sawāka and God could have made him other than a man; the giraffe example and a poetic comparison support this. Alternatively, it is a second object of sawāka, implying ṣayyaraka or jaʿalaka, as al-Ḥawfī holds.
SAMIN-DURR:18:37/r2.anchor: " رجلا " فيه وجهان، أحدهما: أنه حال، وجاز ذلك وإن [كان] غير منتقل

ZAJJAJ:v3p285/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p285/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p285/r6.claim: The Creator first made the man from dust and a drop, then completed him as a man; doubting resurrection after this is disbelief, and false conjecture is sinful.
ZAJJAJ:v3p285/r6.anchor:
أي ثم أكملك، فأنكرت أمر البعث حتى شككت فيه، وقد أعلمنا أن
الشاك

ZAJJAJ:v3p285/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p285/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p285/r7.claim: The companion cites the warning that those who think creation of heaven and earth was purposeless are unbelievers facing the Fire.
ZAJJAJ:v3p285/r7.anchor: وما خلقنا السماء والأرض وما بينهما باطلا ذلك ظن الذين كفروا

ASAD-NOTES:18:37#n44/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:37#n44/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:37#n44/r1.claim: Asad directs readers to his discussions of the creation-from-dust statement at 3:59 and 23:12.
ASAD-NOTES:18:37#n44/r1.anchor: See second half of note 47 on 3:59, and note 4 orr 23:12.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177/r4.claim: وهو يحاوره is a circumstantial clause describing the believing companion as speaker.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177/r4.anchor: وهو يحاوره حال من الفاعل وهو صاحبه المؤمن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177/r5.speaker: أبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177/r5.claim: Ubayy's و هو يخاصمه is an explanatory reading, not a transmitted recitation, since it differs from the codex; the received reading is يحاوره.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبي وهو يخاصمه وهي قراءة تفسير لا قراءة رواية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177/r6.claim: أكفرت is a rebuking question because the man associated another with God; the reminder of creation from dust and a drop proves resurrection is possible and promised by truthful messengers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177/r6.anchor: وأ كفرت استفهام إنكار وتوبيخ حيث أشرك مع الله غيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177/r7.speaker: ثابت البناني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177/r7.claim: Thabit al-Bunani's addition ويلك أكفرت explains the force of the rebuke but is not a Prophetic reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177/r7.anchor: وقرأ ثابت البناني: ويلك أكفرت وهو تفسير معنى التوبيخ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177/r8.claim: خلقك من تراب may refer to Adam, the man's origin, or to his father's food-derived semen before the later drop; a report that an angel puts dust into the semen needs a sound basis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p177/r8.anchor: وقوله خلقك من تراب إما أن يراد خلق أصلك من تراب وهو آدم عليه السلام

BURHAN:v4p430/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p430/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p430/r1.claim: The Qur'an's light form of the emphatic nūn occurs in only two places, one being لنسفعا بالناصية.
BURHAN:v4p430/r1.anchor: ولم يقع التأكيد بالخفيفة في القرآن إلا في موضعين

BURHAN:v4p430/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p430/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p430/r5.claim: The hāʾ may be an ordinary pronoun used in genitive or accusative positions, as in قال له صاحبه وهو يحاوره.

ITQAN:v2p521#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p521#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p521#3/r1.claim: The hāʾ can be a third-person pronoun used in genitive or accusative positions, as in the phrase meaning his companion said to him.
ITQAN:v2p521#3/r1.anchor: اسم ضمير غائب يستعمل في الجر والنصب نحو ﴿ قال له صاحبه وهو يحاوره ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p392/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p392/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p392/r5.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الصاحب في القرآن على تسعة أوجه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p633/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p633/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p633/r2.claim: With ḍamma, thumma is a conjunction marking order with delay, as in 2:28 and 18:37; with fatḥa, thamma is an adverb meaning “there,” as in 26:64.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p633/r2.anchor: ثُمّ بضمّ الثاء هي حرف عطف تفيد الترتيب والتراخي
